summary: Deprecated audit trail for DpcWatchdogPeriod. The current app writes HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Kernel\DpcWatchdogPeriod = 120000, but later KVM current-build evidence tightened the picture sharply: the running kernel currently holds `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0`, `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` only emits the field when it is non-zero, `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` is the explicit writer that updates the global from caller-supplied validated input, a class-focused live KD pass now ties that writer to an admin-gated `NtSetSystemInformation` arm inferred as numeric `0xE4`, a later query-side KD pass confirms the exact outer wrapper `NtQuerySystemInformation+0x8c -> ExpQuerySystemInformation` while leaving the inner watchdog query arm unresolved, Microsoft still documents `KeQueryDpcWatchdogInformation` plus `KDPC_WATCHDOG_INFORMATION` zero-as-disabled semantics, and a later Ghidra init-semantics pass shows that zero-valued watchdog globals can survive current-build initialization. This still does not capture a primary Microsoft source for the exact registry value semantics, so the record remains deprecated.

setting.name: DPC Watchdog Period
setting.casual_explanation: Windows has a watchdog that looks for deferred procedure calls that run too long and can trigger a system crash if the system stays stuck at high interrupt levels. This is a very low-level kernel safety mechanism, not a normal tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: People would only change it when reproducing kernel experiments, undoing manual registry changes, or doing specialized driver debugging.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Changing watchdog timing can affect how quickly Windows decides a DPC path has stalled badly enough to stop the system. This record now has stronger current-build kernel proof than before, but it still lacks a primary Microsoft source for the exact registry key and also conflicts with the app's 120000 baseline.
setting.professional_notes: Microsoft documents that Windows implements a DPC watchdog timer and that a DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (0x133) bug check occurs if a DPC routine or a series of DPC routines runs too long. Microsoft also provides driver guidance for avoiding DPC watchdog timeouts in storport miniports. Earlier decompilation already showed `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs` being read into the watchdog configuration block, but later KVM current-build work tightened the interpretation substantially. A dedicated live bundle read `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0` on the running current build. A later KD disassembly pass then showed that `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` only emits the period field when the global is non-zero, while `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` is the explicit writer that updates `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs` from caller-supplied validated input before `KiCreateDpcLimitsProcessorConfiguration` converts it into processor-local limits. A later class-focused live KD pass then confirmed the exact runtime writer edge at `NtSetSystemInformation+0x1bc9 -> KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, showed that the writer arm is admin-gated via `SeAliasAdminsSid` membership and `RtlCheckTokenMembership`, and exposed dispatch arithmetic that implies numeric system-information arm `0xE4`. A later dedicated query-side KD pass then confirmed the exact outer wrapper edge `NtQuerySystemInformation+0x8c -> ExpQuerySystemInformation` on the same current build, but the captured `ExpQuerySystemInformation` slice still did not isolate a symbolized `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` callsite. That narrows the query-side gap from “no live query lineage” to “inner ExpQuerySystemInformation watchdog arm unresolved.” Microsoft's current WDM documentation now also adds a public zero-state clue that was missing from the earlier audit trail: `KeQueryDpcWatchdogInformation` remains documented, and `KDPC_WATCHDOG_INFORMATION` explicitly says `DpcTimeLimit` becomes `0` when DPC time-out has been disabled and `DpcWatchdogLimit` becomes `0` when the DPC watchdog has been disabled. That does not prove the `DpcWatchdogPeriod` registry value or the exact internal translation from `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs` into the public structure, but it does show that zero-valued public watchdog limits are legitimate in current Microsoft documentation rather than inherently contradictory. A later PDB-backed Ghidra init-semantics pass then showed that `KiInitDpcThresholds` preserves zero-valued watchdog globals unless they are already non-zero and too small, which means the observed live zero period is structurally compatible with current-build initialization rather than just an unexplained contradiction. That leaves the current app baseline `DpcWatchdogPeriod = 120000` in direct tension with live current-build state and with the current-build init/runtime story, not merely unsupported by a primary Microsoft registry source. The record therefore stays deprecated: the registry mapping is still not primary-sourced, the observed live default does not match the repo/app baseline, and the now-confirmed runtime writer path still lacks a proven persisted registry seeding caller.

evidence.title: Microsoft Learn: KeQueryDpcWatchdogInformation function
evidence.summary: Microsoft documents that Windows implements a DPC watchdog timer and describes how the system detects prolonged DPC execution and can bug check with DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (0x133). The page confirms the feature area but does not publish the DpcWatchdogPeriod registry key.

evidence.title: Microsoft Learn: Avoiding DPC Watchdog timeout problems in StorPort Miniports
evidence.summary: Microsoft documents the DPC watchdog feature from the driver-behavior side and explains that Windows can decide a prolonged high-IRQL routine has taken excessive time to finish. The page confirms the watchdog feature area but does not publish the registry key.

evidence.title: Microsoft Learn: KDPC_WATCHDOG_INFORMATION structure
evidence.summary: Microsoft documents the public DPC watchdog result structure and explicitly states that `DpcTimeLimit` is `0` when DPC time-out has been disabled and `DpcWatchdogLimit` is `0` when the DPC watchdog has been disabled.

evidence.title: Decompiled DPC watchdog configuration reader
evidence.summary: The decompiled watchdog configuration reader checks KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs and copies it into the result block when present, proving the raw registry-backed period is consumed by kernel code.

evidence.title: Repo system research notes for kernel registry values
evidence.summary: The repo documents DpcWatchdogPeriod = 120000 as personal research and ties it to KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs.

evidence.title: Current app implementation
evidence.summary: The provider writes DpcWatchdogPeriod = 120000 for the current tweak.

evidence.title: Current-build KVM local-KD shows live DpcWatchdogPeriod state plus reader/writer path
evidence.summary: Dedicated KVM local-KD work read `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0` on the running current build, showed that `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` only emits the field when the global is non-zero, and then showed that `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` is the explicit writer for the global.

evidence.title: Current-build KVM local-KD ties DPC watchdog writer to a privileged NtSetSystemInformation arm
evidence.summary: A class-focused live KVM local-KD pass confirmed `NtSetSystemInformation+0x1bc9 -> KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, showed that the branch is gated by `SeAliasAdminsSid` membership via `RtlCheckTokenMembership`, and exposed dispatch arithmetic that implies numeric writer arm `0xE4`.

evidence.title: PDB-backed KVM Ghidra shows current-build init semantics preserve zero watchdog globals
evidence.summary: A PDB-backed current-build Ghidra pass showed that `KiInitDpcThresholds` only clamps low non-zero watchdog values and therefore allows `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0` to survive initialization, instead of forcing a non-zero default.

evidence.title: Current-build KVM local-KD confirms outer DPC watchdog query wrapper
evidence.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD pass confirmed `NtQuerySystemInformation+0x8c -> ExpQuerySystemInformation` on the running build, but the captured `ExpQuerySystemInformation` slice did not yet isolate a symbolized `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` callsite.

decision.why: Microsoft clearly documents the DPC watchdog feature, but this research pass still did not capture a primary Microsoft source for the DpcWatchdogPeriod registry value itself and the later current-build KD/Ghidra work now shows that the app baseline conflicts with both live kernel state and the current-build init/runtime writer story.
